summary: Xiaoling Wu was a sinologist and Indologist. He was a research scholar and lecturer at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), taught at Peking University (~1946–1949), and served as a professor at Academia Sinica (~1950–1977) and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoting Wei works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under supervisor Kathy Ku Cheng Mei, attested in 2004.

Xinchuan Huang was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1953–1958). He had a long tenure at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–2021; researcher ~1977–1998) and taught Jiang Yili.

Xinru Liu specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher (~1980–1985), was a professor at CASS (1993), and became professor emeritus at The College of New Jersey (~1999).
Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

Xu Dishan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist, and religious studies. Educated at Yenching, Columbia, and Oxford, he held posts at Peking University (~1927–1935), Tsinghua University (~1927–1935), and The University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941), teaching D. C. Lau.

Xuesong Zhang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2008) and served as an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, and studied under Shoryu Katsura. He was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011) and a research associate at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2017).

Y. Karunadasa, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, earned a BA from the University of Ceylon and a PhD from London under David Friedman. He directed the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and was emeritus professor at Kelaniya (~2000).

Yael Bentor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University, where Gregory Schopen was her doctoral supervisor, she held a teaching post in Indian Studies at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2000).
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. She earned a PhD from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.

Yang Renshan was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), the Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and the Buddhist Research Society (1910), which he headed, while teaching figures such as Tan Sitong and Taixu.
Yang-Gyu An specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under doctoral supervisor Richard Gombrich, and also studied under Ven. Hojin (attested 2003).
Yangdon Dhondup is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London between approximately 2000 and 2004 under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi, with Hsing Yun as a traditional teacher (attested 2012).
Yanpei was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Taixu (~1934–1937) and Yin Shun (~1941–1947).
Yao Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He received traditional instruction from Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2010).

Yaroslav Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes and the University of Virginia, later holding a Mellon postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (attested 2011).
